findings.reason: The protected Accepted solution is correct and linear-time but allocates an $O(n)$ ancestor stack. The source explicitly asks for constant extra space; the inert candidate answers that follow-up by reusing the consumed `preorder` prefix as the same monotonic stack, with `top` and `lower_bound` as its only auxiliary state.

The candidate preserves the canonical lower-bound invariant and one-push/one-pop traversal while reducing auxiliary space to $O(1)$. Its deliberate tradeoff is mutation of `preorder`, which the Approach states explicitly; the app-local parameter and Boolean return contract remain unchanged.

The protected app-local and immutable Accepted native sources remain structurally aligned as the same separate-stack algorithm and submission evidence is unchanged. The candidate is intentionally inert and differs only by storing that same logical stack in the consumed input prefix.

The benchmark's former zero-based increasing values violated the source minimum of one. Legal 32/128/512-node increasing preorders now expose repeated recursive suffix validation. The candidate passes at +0.04 relative exponent with a 1.34x largest runtime ratio; a correct recursive range-partition implementation passes every output and fails only scaling at +1.13 with a 119.98x ratio.

The Approach now describes the candidate exactly: the consumed prefix stores the active decreasing ancestor path, the last pop establishes the permanent lower bound, future unread values are never overwritten, and input mutation is the explicit constant-space tradeoff.
The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against the source structure, preserving both factual examples, all three constraints, and the constant-extra-space follow-up.
